oracle.definitions: Let a[i,d] in {0,1} indicate correctness of already recorded answer for item i and fixed depth d in D={1,3,5}. For any single-output selector s(i) in D, a[i,s(i)] <= max_d a[i,d] pointwise. Summing and dividing by N preserves <=. If every d is wrong, maximum is0; otherwise selecting minimum-cost correct d attains1 for this fixed item.
oracle.limits: This is an accuracy upper bound over the fixed output trace; cheapest correct cost is only conditional on its recorded candidate answers and known gold. Computing all answers to discover which is correct has extra search cost. Different sampling/weights/new items are outside the bound.

recorded_trace_check.scope: Accuracy upper bound for choosing one of the recorded outputs, with true labels available. Does not price search or predict generalization.

cost.formula: T_total = T_controller + T_solver + T_other; saving delta_solver can be outweighed when delta_controller+delta_other > delta_solver.
cost.example_scope: Algebraic possibility; does not assume proportionality of solver loop count to wall time. Both real fixed modes and real Auto here also use two C calls.

memory.formula: Static parameter bytes = sum(numel(p)*element_size(p)); inference peak includes simultaneously alive parameters, activations, temporary tensors and runtime allocator effects.
memory.limits: No CPU/GPU peak was measured here. This only verifies the distinction requested by the text.
